01.r: Forbids the act as a wish or warning: do not do it.
01.n: The brief's lexicon gives this negative as 'not' of wish or preference: do not, let not. Gesenius compares Greek μή.

02.r: To take payment from the borrower.

03.r: From the poor brother of the verse before.
03.n: Literally 'from with him', two prepositions together, which BDB gives as from proximity with someone.

04.n: Gesenius and BDB both give interest, usury. We render it 'interest' everywhere (see Exodus 22:25 on this page) and keep 'increase' for the next word, so the two Hebrew words stay apart.

05.r: A second kind of gain from a loan, named beside interest.
05.n: Gesenius: from the root רָבָה, interest, usury, the same as מַרְבִּית (the word in Leviticus 25:37 on this page), and he cites this verse. BDB: increment, interest, usury. The lexicons in the brief do not say how it differed from the word before it; 'increase' follows the root and keeps the two apart.

s: you shall stand in awe of
06.r: Reverence for God is what stops the lender from exploiting his brother.
06.n: A perfect with 'and', which carries on the command: 'and you shall fear'. Gesenius gives the root sense as TO TREMBLE. YLT renders the perfect form literally, 'thou hast been afraid'.

07.r: Your own God, the one who sees how you lend.
07.n: Literally 'fear from your God': Hebrew can join this verb to its object with 'from'. English says 'fear your God'. The form is plural but the meaning is singular.

08.r: The poor brother keeps his life and his place among you.
08.n: Another perfect with 'and': literally 'and your brother shall live with you'. Most translations read it as the purpose of the law, 'that he may live'; the Hebrew joins it with a plain 'and'.

09.r: A fellow Israelite, counted as family.
09.n: The brief's lexicon lists brother of the same parents, relative, and one of the same tribe. The BSB's 'countryman' takes the wider sense.

10.r: Alongside the lender, in the same community.

_extra.12: ἐγὼ (I): begins 'I am the Lord', added by the Greek translators.
_extra.13: κύριος (Lord): part of the added 'I am the Lord'.

04.n: τόκος, interest; the word also means offspring.

05.n: πλῆθος, a great number, abundance: 'nor in abundance'. The first word is printed οὐ in our Greek text, with dictionary form οὐδέ, 'nor'; it is likely οὐδέ cut short.

08.n: Our Greek text has only καὶ here, 'and your brother with you', with no verb for 'shall live'. It may be a word lost in the machine reading; we cannot tell from the brief.
